title: Restriction to a localized ringed site preserves K-injectivity
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with Grothendieck topology $J$, $\mathcal R$ a sheaf of rings with section modules in universe $\max(u,v)$, and $U\in\mathcal C$. Let $I$ be a K-injective cochain complex of $\mathcal R$-modules [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Its termwise restriction $I|_U$ to $\mathcal C/U$ is K-injective. Restriction sends zero morphisms to zero; its proof is an explicit parameter used only to form the functor on complexes.

proof.text: Use the exact additive finite-limit and finite-colimit left adjunction supplied by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized-adjunction]. The adjunction induces preservation of K-injective complexes by its right adjoint, so applying that preservation theorem to I yields K-injectivity after restriction.

theorem isKInjective_restrict_localized
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{max u v}) (U : C)
    (hzero : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{max u v} R U).PreservesZeroMorphisms)
    (I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{max u v} R) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective] :
    letI := hzero
    CochainComplex.IsKInjective
      (((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{max u v} R U).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I)
